title: A 37-Year Soil Experiment Revealed a Hidden Climate Threat
hook: The world's longest-running soil warming experiment just found that warming can unlock carbon scientists thought was safely locked away underground.
key_points: Researchers have kept a soil-warming experiment running continuously for 37 years — the longest of its kind.
Scientists had long assumed a large share of soil carbon is chemically stabilized and effectively protected from decomposition, even as temperatures rise.
After nearly four decades, warming caused microbes to break down that supposedly stable carbon anyway, releasing extra CO2.
This points to a feedback loop — warming frees stored soil carbon, which drives further warming — that current climate models may be underestimating.
content_html: For 37 years, one research team has kept a patch of soil artificially warmed — the longest-running experiment of its kind. It just delivered an unwelcome surprise.
extra_html: Scientists have long assumed that a large share of carbon stored in soil is chemically stabilized, bound up in ways that protect it from microbial decomposition even as the climate warms. This experiment says otherwise: after nearly four decades of sustained warming, soil microbes broke down carbon that was thought to be safely locked away, releasing extra carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. That matters beyond one field plot, because it points to a feedback loop current climate models may be underestimating — warming frees up stored soil carbon, and that carbon, once in the atmosphere, drives further warming.

related.title: Nutrient Cycles
related.hook: The carbon in your breath, the nitrogen in your DNA, the water in your blood — all of it has cycled through living things and the planet countless times. Nothing is used up; everything is recycled.
